subject: Implementation constraints for private VPC deployment - diagrams & runbook feedback
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Infra Team <infra@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment - initial constraints and questions

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier this week. We started mapping the network constraints from our colo team and ran into a few implementation questions that will affect the control-plane/data-plane split and the reference diagrams you shared: 

- Our colo has a single eBGP pair per rack and we need guidance on how Redwood expects to attach the data-plane fabric (NAT vs. routed VLAN).
- We have a strict outbound proxy requirement for control-plane telemetry (all egress via 10.240.0.1). Can Redwood route control traffic through a separate interface?
- Certificate rotation: we rotate leaf certs every 7 days; what dependencies do you have on CA pushes and how will node restarts be handled during rollout?

I've attached a short PDF summarizing our constraints and a rough sketch from the colo team. Can you confirm whether the control-plane needs an internet-routable egress or if it can be NAT'd behind the tenant edge?

Sasha from our networking team (cc'd) will be the day-to-day contact. Looking to sync by EOD tomorrow if possible.

Thanks,
Daniel
ACME Technologies — Principal Infra Engineer

Attachments: vpc-implementation-constraints.pdf, colo-sketch.png
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment - initial constraints and questions

Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick responses inline: 

- Data-plane attachment: Redwood supports both routed VLANs and NATted attachments. For low-latency inference we recommend routed VLANs (sizable MTU, direct next-hop). NAT is acceptable for early stages but will complicate metrics and KV cache pinning.

- Control-plane egress: the control-plane can be NAT'd behind the tenant edge. We only require outbound connectivity to our control endpoints (api.redwood-inference.com) and to our telemetry ingest; reachable via HTTPS over 443 is sufficient. If you must funnel through 10.240.0.1 that is fine — please confirm TLS inspection is not terminating (we need end-to-end TLS).

- Cert rotation: our control-plane expects an automated CA distribution path (S3/KMS or your internal PKI push). Rolling restarts are safe — nodes rejoin and resync KV caches. We will provide a rotation playbook; short-lived cert windows (7 days) are okay but we will need a 24h buffer to stage the rollout.

We'll need to update the reference diagram to show an optional edge-NAT pattern and an explicit telemetry-proxy hop. I'm looping in Rishi from product infra to capture the required changes to the control/data diagram and to propose an ops-level addendum to the runbook.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Rishi to share a marked-up controlplane/dataflow PNG (today).
2) Kimberly + Marissa to draft a runbook addendum for cert rotations and telemetry NAT (tomorrow).
3) Follow-up sync with Sasha and ACME infra on Mon to approve attachment method.

I'll attach a short diff of the runbook once Rishi posts the diagram.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Attachment references: controlplane-dataflow-sketch.png (pending Rishi), runbook-diff.md
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sasha Klein <sasha.k@colonet.net>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 14:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment - initial constraints and questions

Attaching a quick sketch and an operations note. High-level changes I made to the diagram (see attached PNG):

- Option A (recommended): Routed VLAN to data-plane with dedicated next-hop per rack. Control-plane nodes live in a separate management subnet with NATted egress to the telemetry proxy (10.240.0.1).
- Option B (fallback): NAT both planes behind edge box; adds complexity for token-bucket KV affinity and inflates latency under cache-miss.

Critical implementation constraints called out on the PNG and in the PDF: 
- MTU 9000 recommended on data-plane links for model artifact transfer.
- Avoid TLS inspection on control-plane egress. We rely on end-to-end mTLS for control messages.
- If ACME PKI pushes certs, ensure a staging copy is available to Redwood to validate before cutover (we can accept an SFTP drop or presigned S3 uplink).

Ops note (short): during cert rotation we perform rolling drain of control-plane nodes with a soft-failover timeout of 90s to avoid cache eviction storms. The runbook diff lists the exact kubectl drain sequence and fallback commands.

Daniel / Sasha — quick questions for ACME: 
- Can you confirm MTU and whether jumbo frames are enabled across the colo fabric?
- Will the telemetry proxy perform outbound TLS passthrough or terminate?

If you confirm MTU and passthrough, we can finalize the diagram and the runbook addendum tomorrow and produce a single PDF (v1) for your procurement packet.

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Product Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: controlplane-dataflow-sketch.png, vpc-implementation-constraints.pdf, runbook-diff.md
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>, Sasha Klein <sasha.k@colonet.net>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment - implementation constraints and next steps

Daniel / Sasha — thank you for the quick turn. Confirmations below and next steps: 

- Sasha confirmed MTU 9000 across the target racks and that the colo fabric will allow routed VLANs (quoted from Sasha: "we can present a routed adjacency; no NAT required at first cut").
- Telemetry proxy will do TLS passthrough (no termination). Sasha: please share the proxy IPs and any ACLs we need to accommodate.

Given those confirmations, we're moving forward with Option A (routed VLAN for data-plane + NATted control-plane egress via 10.240.0.1 with TLS passthrough). Rishi will finish the diagram and I'll assemble the runbook v1 (controls, cert rotation, and acceptance tests).

Deliverables & tentative timeline: 
- Rishi: updated PNG and a single combined PDF (control/data + runbook addendum) — Mon 10/05 EOD PT.
- Kimberly: runbook v1 assembled and uploaded to Drive; procurement-ready artifact including the diagram and acceptance checklist — Tue 10/06 EOD PT.
- ACME: provide telemetry proxy IPs, any egress ACLs, and preferred method for staged cert push (SFTP or presigned S3) — by Mon 10/05.

If there are any constraints that prevent Option A, escalate to me directly and we can discuss a short-term NAT fallback. Otherwise we will proceed as planned.

Appreciate the partnership — I'll post the combined PDF and HubSpot note when ready.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)
